highlights.title: Google Shifts AI Leadership to California in Race Against Anthropic, OpenAI
highlights.description: Alphabet Inc.'s Google is concentrating its artificial intelligence leadership at its Mountain View, California, headquarters to gain momentum in the accelerating race against Anthropic and OpenAI to build the world’s dominant AI models.

highlights.title: Meta's New Mac Coding Agent Costs Up to 20x Less If You Let Meta Train on Your Data
highlights.description:
Meta today launched Muse Code, a terminal coding agent available for macOS and Linux. Muse Code is in beta, and it is powered by Muse Spark 1.2, ‌Meta‌'s newest model.


‌Meta‌ CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse Code can accomplish complete software engineering tasks across large repos. It can plan out changes, write code, and validate results using multiple persistent subagents.

Muse Code is ‌Meta‌'s equivalent of OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code, and it is ‌Meta‌'s first major push into agentic coding.

There are several default skills available, such as /plan for turning a task into an approval-gated plan, /grill for stress testing a plan, and /goal for working toward the successful completion of an objective. Muse Code maintains an append-only local event log of every model call, tool run, approval, and edit, so it can resume where it stopped if it crashes.

Muse Code can be used through the Mac's terminal after a one-command install, and there is no dedicated app available. The model is priced at $1.25 for 1 million input tokens and $4.25 for 1 million output tokens, but ‌Meta‌ is offering a discount for users who give the company permission to use their prompts and completions to train future AI models.

With the Contributor tier enabled for ‌Meta‌ model training, Muse Spark 1.2 is priced at $0.10 for 1 million input tokens and $0.20 for 1 million output tokens. The Standard tier costs more and does not let ‌Meta‌ use prompts to train its models.

highlights.title: OpenAI Asks Judge to Toss Apple’s Trade Secrets Lawsuit
highlights.description: OpenAI is asking a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit filed by Apple Inc. accusing the artificial intelligence company of stealing trade secrets, saying that the iPhone maker’s allegations are meritless.

highlights.title: SoftBank Profit Beats Expectations
highlights.description: SoftBank Group Corp. reported a smaller-than-expected decline in quarterly net income, helped by a rally in its chip-stock holdings. OpenAI’s Japanese backer is in the spotlight alongside concerns about climbing debt levels that AI service providers are taking on to spend on data centers and other infrastructure. Bloomberg's Neil Campling reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Cybersecurity firm Aura CEO on 2Q26 Results
highlights.description: Hari Ravinchandran, Founder and CEO of cyber-security platform Aura, discusses his outlook for the company's growth at it reported a 27-percent year-on-year increase in pro forma revenue. He says the firm is on track to generate positive free cash flow this year, following its acquisition of tech firm Qoria and its listing on the Australian Securities Exchange. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Elon Musk’s attempt at an AI Wikipedia hasn’t been updated in months
highlights.description:
xAI's Grokipedia, an online encyclopedia with AI-generated articles that Elon Musk once promised would be a "massive improvement" over Wikipedia, apparently hasn't been updated since April 24th, according to a report from Lawfare. "As far as we can tell, no entry has changed in more than three months," Lawfare said.
